clue.text: Girl that is getting second teeth

parts.note: Pearl is a girl's name
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A girl whose adult teeth are coming through.
explanation.walkthrough: PEARLIES is informal slang for teeth, from their whiteness; 'getting' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearlies is a jokey slang name for white teeth, likening them to pearls.

clue.text: Dutch cheese and English crackers brought over

indicators.note: brought over suggests turning the word for crackers round so it reads the other way

parts.note: crackers is slang for mad

explanation.surface: A cheese board with Dutch cheese and English crackers carried across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like biscuits to go with the cheese, but it means mad; 'brought over' turns that word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild round cheese from the Netherlands, usually sold in red wax.

clue.text: Work hard in effort to get medal

indicators.note: in tells us the work and hard pieces sit inside the word for effort

parts.note: a try is an attempt or effort
op, short for opus, is a work of art or music
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An athlete trains hard and strains to win a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is the musical opus, abbreviated; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a prize awarded for winning, much as a medal is.

clue.text: Defector — a petty officer, say

parts.note: PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer
to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: A naval petty officer who has deserted to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is a verb here, STATE, not the usual 'for example' signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a faith or cause, a deserter from belief.

clue.text: Band's to touch down where the gold coast is

parts.note: Queen is the British rock band, so the band's gives the possessive form
to land an aircraft is to touch down

explanation.surface: A rock band's plane is due to touch down on a sunny coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gold Coast is a resort strip in this Australian state; the clue lower-cases it to hide the proper name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gold Coast holiday region lies in the north-east Australian state on the Pacific.

clue.text: Runs onto a jetty producing sword

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
a pier is a jetty projecting into water

explanation.surface: Someone runs onto a jetty and pulls out a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onto' and 'producing' simply join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender thrusting sword used in fencing and duelling.

clue.text: Police officer in Paris given info on armed criminal

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: criminal suggests the following word is bent out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A French policeman is briefed about an armed criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun in the surface, but it is the anagram signal working on 'armed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the French national police force.

clue.text: Straighten out former nurse

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: Someone sets a former nurse straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an arm or leg is to straighten it out fully.

clue.text: More than one mate interrupted by pointless draw

indicators.note: interrupted by means the word for mate is split open with another piece put in

parts.note: a pal is a mate or friend

indicators.note: pointless asks us to drop a compass point, here E for east, from the word for draw

parts.note: to lure is to draw or entice

explanation.surface: A chess partner is held to yet another tame draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes a compass point, east; 'interrupted by' then splits the friend to take what is left of the draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural is the grammatical term for referring to more than a single thing.

clue.text: Daughter's peculiar house

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A daughter's home is a strange place.
explanation.walkthrough: DRUM is old British slang for a house or flat.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a drum is one's home or dwelling place.

clue.text: Fancy cakes and fancy a pie? Resist

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborately altered, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dieter tempted by pastries is told to resist the pie.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'fancy' signals an anagram of A PIE RESIST; the first is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a shop selling, or a collection of, French pastries and sweet bakes.

clue.text: Unhappiness caused by penny-pincher at end of holiday

parts.note: a miser is a stingy penny-pincher

indicators.note: at end of points to the final letter of the word holiday

explanation.surface: The gloom of a tight-fisted traveller when the holiday is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Misery is a state of deep distress or wretchedness.

clue.text: Noblemen curry favour in exhibition centre

parts.note: earls are noblemen of the British peerage
to court someone is to seek their favour

explanation.surface: Aristocrats sucking up to someone at a trade show.
explanation.walkthrough: EARLS COURT is a former exhibition centre in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls Court was a large London venue that hosted shows and trade fairs.

clue.text: Refuge for couples, small number on a hot island

parts.note: No. is the short form of number
H is the tap abbreviation for hot
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A tiny hot island offers a retreat for a few honeymoon couples.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is a small Channel Island between England and France. The animals entered the vessel two by two, hence 'couples'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the vessel sheltered animals in pairs from the flood.

clue.text: Writer's attribute article ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the article is left out of the word for attribute

parts.note: to attribute something to someone is to ascribe it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An author's characteristic quality is overlooked in a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attribute' is a verb, not a noun; 'Writer's' reads as 'Writer is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is someone who copies or writes documents by hand, a professional penman.

clue.text: More in base worried

indicators.note: in shows the word for more goes inside the word for base

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as in a flower bed or seabed
other can mean additional or more, as in other examples

explanation.surface: Someone anxious at a military base wants more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' suggests a military base, but it is a bed in the sense of a foundation; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothered describes someone troubled or anxious.

clue.text: A politician follows vicar and tart up

indicators.note: follows means the article and politician come after the vicar

parts.note: Rev., Reverend, is the title of a vicar
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A politician trails a vicar and a woman of easy virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart up' means smarten, not a woman or a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp is to renovate or give a new look, as tarting up does.

clue.text: Rustic finished exam

parts.note: past means over or finished
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin has passed the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral means relating to the countryside and rural life.

clue.text: Rope carried by Pete, the rancher

indicators.note: carried by means the answer is borne within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A lasso slung over the shoulder of Pete the rancher.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope or chain tying an animal to a post.

clue.text: Put in order for tape

indicators.note: in tells us the word for put goes inside the word for order

parts.note: a caste is a social order or class
to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: An instruction to put something in order for recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in order' reads like one phrase but splits: 'in' is the container signal between put and order.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a sealed case holding magnetic recording tape.

clue.text: Everyone in position and ready to start

parts.note: all means everyone
set means placed or fixed in position

explanation.surface: Runners all on their marks, poised for the off.
explanation.definitionFit: All set is an idiom meaning fully prepared to begin.

clue.text: Salad plant artist's shown on plate

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard crossword artist
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: A painter's salad served on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown on' simply joins RA to DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a pungent root vegetable eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Fish seen round mouth of river? It's a wonder

indicators.note: round means the fish encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish

indicators.note: mouth of points to the opening letter of the word river

parts.note: taken as the word it

explanation.surface: A fish spotted at a river mouth is something to marvel at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' makes the fish enclose the river's first letter and the word it; the question mark hides that the clue runs on.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is something uncommon and remarkable, a marvel.

clue.text: Later, he got drunk (completely)

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling and jumbled

explanation.surface: Afterwards he got totally drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' signals an anagram of LATER HE GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means entirely or in total.

clue.text: Pick out son with cup

parts.note: a pot is a trophy cup

explanation.surface: Choosing a son along with a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or identify it.

clue.text: Appear in musical

definitions.meaning: to appear is to turn up or become visible
a stage musical is a theatrical production

explanation.surface: Someone appears in a stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up is to appear, and a show is a theatre production such as a musical.

clue.text: Tries starter of estate car

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court

indicators.note: starter of points to the opening letter of the word estate

explanation.surface: Someone test-drives the first estate car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' is a judge trying a case, HEARS, not testing a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin at a funeral.

clue.text: Reasonable grounds detailed

indicators.note: detailed read as de-tailed means cutting off the final letter

parts.note: a rationale is the grounds or reasons for something

explanation.surface: Sensible grounds set out in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as 'de-tailed': drop the last letter of RATIONALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means sensible and based on reason.
